title: Find the Maximum Number of Fruits Collected
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every pair of routes for the two outer children is exponential. The moves themselves remove the difficulty:

- The child from `(0, 0)` must cover `n - 1` rows and `n - 1` columns in `n - 1` moves, so every move is diagonal: it walks the main diagonal and collects all of it.
- The child from `(0, n - 1)` goes down one row per move, so it is in row `i` after `i` moves. To still reach column `n - 1` it can never be left of the diagonal, so away from the diagonal it only visits the upper triangle.
- The child from `(n - 1, 0)` is its mirror image and only visits the lower triangle.

So the three routes never share a room off the diagonal, and the answer is the diagonal plus two independent best paths. Touching the diagonal gains nothing (it is already emptied), so the top-right child can stay strictly right of it, and a row-by-row grid DP finds its best path.

## Approach

1. Add every `fruits[i][i]` to `total`.
2. In `topRight(grid)`, `dp[j]` is the most the child can hold standing in column `j` of the current row; only `dp[n - 1] = grid[0][n - 1]` is reachable at row 0.
3. For each row `i` from `1` to `n - 2`, each column `j` from `max(i + 1, n - 1 - i)` to `n - 1` takes the best of `dp[j - 1]`, `dp[j]`, `dp[j + 1]` plus `grid[i][j]`.
4. At row `n - 2` only column `n - 1` is right of the diagonal; `dp[n - 1]` is the haul (the last room is on the diagonal).
5. Transposing the grid turns the bottom-left child into a top-right one, so add `topRight(transposed)`.

## Example 1, step by step

The diagonal gives `1 + 6 + 11 + 16 = 34`. Top-right child: `dp[3] = 4`; row 1 gives `next[2] = 4 + 8 = 12` and `next[3] = 4 + 7 = 11`; row 2 gives `dp[3] = 12 + 12 = 24`. On the transposed grid: `13`, then `23` and `27`, then `27 + 15 = 42`. Total: `34 + 24 + 42 = 100`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each DP visits each cell of its triangle once.
- Space: O(n²) for the transposed copy; `dp` itself is O(n).

## Pitfalls

- Columns left of `n - 1 - i` cannot be reached in `i` moves; they must stay `-Infinity`, never `0`.
- Do not add room `(n - 1, n - 1)` again: the diagonal already counted it.
- Picking the richest next room greedily is not optimal; the DP compares all routes.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total` | fruits on the main diagonal |
| `dp[j]`, `next[j]` | best haul ending in column `j` of the previous / current row |
| `best` | best of the three rooms the child can come from |
| `transposed` | the grid flipped across its diagonal |
